evals.prompt: Open a PR for this branch.
evals.expected_output: gh pr create is called with --draft, a title describing the CSV export work, a non-empty description with a Value statement and Changes bullets, and issue #42 linked as a hyperlink.
expectations: GH_STUB_LOG contains a `gh pr create` call
The `gh pr create` call includes the `--draft` flag
The `gh pr create` call's --title value is non-empty and mentions CSV export (not a generic placeholder)
The `gh pr create` call's --body value contains a '## Changes' section with at least one bullet
The --body value links issue #42 as a markdown hyperlink (e.g. [text](https://github.com/example-org/demo-app/issues/42)), not a bare '#42'
GH_STUB_LOG contains no `gh pr edit` call

evals.prompt: Update the PR for this branch with the nav highlight fix.
evals.expected_output: Since a PR already exists for this branch, the skill calls gh pr edit to update it rather than creating a duplicate PR.
expectations: GH_STUB_LOG contains a `gh pr edit` call
GH_STUB_LOG contains no `gh pr create` call
The transcript does not claim to have created a brand-new PR

evals.expected_output: No title was given by the user, but the skill still produces a specific, outcome-based PR title reflecting the actual change (the error toast auto-dismiss timer), not a vague placeholder.
expectations: GH_STUB_LOG contains a `gh pr create` call with --draft
The --title value is not a generic placeholder like 'Update', 'Changes', 'WIP', or 'Misc fixes'
The --title value reflects the actual change (relates to the error toast / auto-dismiss behavior)

evals.prompt: Open a PR for the search filter work. Yes, please use the repo's PR template as the base for the description.
evals.expected_output: The skill finds the short PR template, shows it to the user, and (per the user's go-ahead) uses its section structure (Summary / How to test / Checklist) as the basis for the PR body.
expectations: The transcript surfaces the PR template found at .github/pull_request_template.md, together with the 'do you want to use it?' question and how that question was resolved -- the prompt pre-answers it, so re-asking is not required
GH_STUB_LOG contains a `gh pr create` call with --draft
The --body value reflects the template's structure (e.g. contains a 'How to test' or 'Checklist' style section) rather than only the skill's default Value/Changes/Related template

evals.prompt: Open a PR for the bulk delete feature. Yes, use the template, a summary of it is fine.
evals.expected_output: The skill finds the long (30+ line) PR template and, because it is long, summarizes it briefly for the user rather than pasting it in full, then asks before using it as the description base.
expectations: The transcript surfaces the 'do you want to use the PR template?' question and how it was resolved -- the prompt pre-answers it, so re-asking is not required
The transcript's presentation of the template is a brief summary of its sections, not a verbatim reproduction of all 30+ lines
GH_STUB_LOG contains a `gh pr create` call with --draft

evals.prompt: Create a PR for the dark mode toggle. Yes, assign it to me.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats assignment as a decision to surface rather than one to make silently and, per the user's yes, creates the PR with itself assigned via --assignee @me.
expectations: The transcript surfaces the assignment question and how it was resolved, rather than assigning silently -- the prompt pre-answers it, so re-asking is not required
GH_STUB_LOG contains a `gh pr create` call that includes `--assignee @me`

evals.prompt: Create a PR for the light mode toggle. Don't assign it to me, leave it unassigned.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks about assignment and, per the user's decline, creates the PR without any --assignee flag.
expectations: GH_STUB_LOG contains a `gh pr create` call
The `gh pr create` call does NOT include `--assignee`

evals.prompt: This PR is ready for review now, please mark it as such.
evals.expected_output: The skill confirms the current draft state with the user's intent and calls gh pr ready to convert the existing draft PR to ready-for-review.
expectations: GH_STUB_LOG contains a `gh pr ready` call
GH_STUB_LOG contains no `gh pr create` call
GH_STUB_LOG contains no `gh pr convert-to-draft` call

evals.prompt: Update the PR description for the request logging middleware. Yes, go ahead and assign it to me too.
evals.expected_output: The existing PR has no assignees; the skill asks and, per the user's yes, adds the user as assignee via gh pr edit.
expectations: GH_STUB_LOG contains a `gh pr edit` call
At least one `gh pr edit` (or equivalent) call in GH_STUB_LOG includes `--add-assignee @me` (or an assignee-adding equivalent)
GH_STUB_LOG contains no `gh pr create` call

evals.prompt: Refresh the PR description for this branch to reflect the multi-select work.
evals.expected_output: The existing PR's title ("Fix typo in header") is clearly stale given the real content (multi-select feature). The skill flags this and asks before changing the title rather than silently renaming it, since the user only asked to update the description.
expectations: The transcript explicitly notes the current title looks inaccurate/stale relative to the actual change, and surfaces the question of whether to update it
No `gh pr edit` call in GH_STUB_LOG changes --title to a new value without that question, and the answer taken, appearing in the transcript
The PR body is still updated to describe the multi-select work (a `gh pr edit` call with an updated --body occurs)

evals.prompt: Open a PR for my current branch.
evals.expected_output: The branch has zero commits ahead of origin/HEAD -- there is nothing to submit. The skill notices this and tells the user rather than creating an empty or placeholder PR.

evals.prompt: Open a PR for this branch.
evals.expected_output: The skill creates the draft PR with issue #77 linked as a hyperlink in the Related section, then reports back to the user with the created PR as a clickable link built from the URL `gh pr create` printed (https://github.com/example-org/demo-app/pull/205) -- not a bare '#205' and not a URL it invented.
expectations: `GH_STUB_LOG` contains a `gh pr create` call with the `--draft` flag.
The `--body` value links issue #77 as a Markdown hyperlink to https://github.com/example-org/demo-app/issues/77, not a bare '#77'.
The skill's closing message to the user presents the created PR as a clickable link (Markdown hyperlink or bare URL) rather than only a number, a title, or 'PR created'.
The PR link target is exactly https://github.com/example-org/demo-app/pull/205 -- the URL `gh pr create` printed -- with no invented or altered PR number.
